summary: The account came back to life on the client's side, not ALTR's. Volume went from 4 messages last week to 42 this week, and 28 of those 42 are Vale's. She restarted work unprompted — 'Also I submitted a a new set on the Google Docs' (Aug 29) and 'Uploaded more feed posts and ppv pics' (Aug 31) — despite the sexting-set template and content brief Ollie promised 'in the morning' on Jul 28 still never having been sent, 38 days on. Ollie Mckinlay ended a nine-day silence on Aug 29, but only after Mayson @-tagged him ('@olkmck ^'), and his entire output for the week was eight words across three messages: 'Thank you', 'Will look into this for you', 'Thank you very much'. He has still never acknowledged that John's $2,000 custom was delivered — she uploaded it on Aug 22 and thirteen days later nobody has confirmed the fan received it, or that the $200 ASAP-delivery fee Ollie personally collected on Aug 18 was honoured. That $2,200 remains the largest live chargeback exposure on the account. Two genuinely good things happened. Vale reported a leak surge on Aug 29 ('Hi babe lots of leaks right now') and Michelle answered inside twelve hours with 'got it babes we're on it', with the weekly breakdown landing on cadence on Sep 1. And when Vale raised a new problem on Aug 31 — her Instagram trial reels collapsing from 200k+ reach to under 3k — Mica Vecco diagnosed it the same evening and handed her a concrete three-variant hook test. That is the best piece of ALTR work on this account in a month. Against that: Stephski issued the Sep 1 invoice on time but skipped the pre-invoice OF-withdrawal reminder that has preceded every recent cycle (Aug 14, Jun 30, May 13), and she has now gone 18 days without confirming receipt of Vale's Aug 17 payment — against an account number that changed on that very invoice. Not one of the twelve carried-over commitments moved. The girl-girl vault purge is 33 days unconfirmed, the written PPV/private-live rule 23 days, the Infloww unauthorized-access enquiry 38 days, Vivek's referral routing 32 days, Mayson's biweekly call 53 days, and the paid backlog — Ryan $600 (90 days), John's $1,800 videocall (126 days), Tyler's $700 custom (152 days) — went a third consecutive week without a single mention by anyone, including Vale. Third clean week on fan trust, and this time the page was busy, so it counts for more than the last two.

health.rationale: Up 4 from 48, and the recovery is narrow and fragile. What improved is contact: ALTR sent 14 messages instead of 1, four different people responded to her the same day, Michelle turned the leak surge around in under twelve hours, Mica delivered a real diagnosis and a testable plan on the IG reach drop, and the Sep 1 invoice went out on time. What did not improve is delivery. Ollie contributed eight words all week and still has not confirmed that John's $2,000 custom — uploaded Aug 22, paid for in May, carrying a $200 rush fee — ever reached the fan; that is 13 days of a $2,200 chargeback exposure sitting unverified. Stephski shipped an invoice without ever acknowledging the previous payment (18 days) and skipped the withdrawal reminder that has preceded every recent cycle. All twelve carried-over commitments simply aged another week: nothing written down on the PPV breach (23 days), nothing confirmed on the vault purge (33 days), nothing booked from the $3,100 paid backlog (90 to 152 days). Held up by a third consecutive week with no fan-trust incident on an active page, and by the client re-engaging hard on her own. Prior scores: 70 (Aug 8), 62 (Aug 14), 60 (Aug 21), 48 (Aug 28).
